claims.text: Metal–support interfacial strain governs the ethanol oxidation performance of the PGM nanoscale catalyst.
Interfacial strain tunes the d-band center of the catalytically active PGM sites.
A strain-induced shift of the d-band center changes the adsorption energies of ethanol-oxidation intermediates.
Changes in intermediate adsorption energies influence catalytic activity, selectivity, and durability.
Post-synthesis annealing in H2 will modify or relax interfacial strain relative to annealing in Ar.
Alteration of interfacial strain modulates the electronic structure and d-band center of PGM sites at the metal–support interface.
H2-atmosphere annealing relieves or modifies excessive strain at the metal–support interface.
The resulting strain adjustment shifts the d-band center of the PGM sites.
A shifted d-band center fine-tunes the binding energies of oxygenated ethanol-oxidation intermediates.
Overly strong intermediate adsorption can poison the catalyst, whereas overly weak adsorption can impede reaction kinetics.
Optimizing intermediate binding will enhance catalytic performance and durability.
Compared with the Ar-treated baseline, the H2-treated catalyst will have a lower ethanol-oxidation onset potential.
Compared with the Ar-treated baseline, the H2-treated catalyst will have higher catalytic current density.
Compared with the Ar-treated baseline, the H2-treated catalyst will show improved product selectivity and cycling stability.
The anticipated performance enhancement is approximately 10–30%.
The proposed mechanism should apply under moderate-temperature, ordinary potential-cycling ethanol-oxidation conditions.
At very high temperatures, excessively high potentials, or under severe structural degradation, other degradation mechanisms may dominate and the proposed relationship may fail.

contradictions.description: The baseline is variously described as a catalyst with unmodified interfacial strain, an Ar-annealed catalyst, and either an untreated or inert-annealed catalyst. Untreated and Ar-annealed materials are not necessarily equivalent, so the control state is internally inconsistent.
